names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 19 Ιουλίου, «Όσιος Θεόδωρος ο Σαββαΐτης επίσκοπος Εδέσσης», with the rank words and the bynames left off. The page gives his father's name as Συμεών and his mother's as Μαρία.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 9. јул ст. ст., „Св. Теодор еп. Едески, и други с њим“ — Св. is not a rank, „еп.“ is the rank, which `types` already carries, and „Едески“ is the see that rank governs and comes off with it; „и други с њим“ names nobody and is no part of his name. The bare forename is left. «of Edessa» in the display name is the corpus’s own. **The fold is forced and four deep before this day**: `foldchk.py` returns `theodore-boyar-of-chernigov`, `theodore-of-perga`, `theodore-of-vrsac` and `theodore-prince-of-yaroslavl`, all `sr`, for «Теодор», so this is the fifth folder on the string, and the heading offers no by-name to break it with — the see in it being a see.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 19ης Ιουλίου — «Όσιος Θεόδωρος ο Σαββαΐτης επίσκοπος Εδέσσης»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 19 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The corpus keeps no Theodore of Edessa and no Sabbaite Theodore: the only Edessene folders are Barses, Barsimaeus, Bassa, Callinicus, Eulogius, Gurias, Samonas, Abibus and John, and the only Sabbaite is Stephen the Sabbaite of 13 July, John of Damascus's nephew, who is a different man with a different life. So this is a new folder and not an upgrade. The page gives no year and no century anywhere, so there is no `dates` object; it says the life was written by Basil bishop of Emesa and that a Greek life survives at the Monastery of Iviron. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. The page prints no hymn, so the folder has none. The `office` is the see the listing itself gives him; the page glosses Edessa as being in the Middle East and says nothing more precise.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 22.07.2026 (9. јул ст. ст.) — „Св. Теодор еп. Едески, и други с њим“

attestations.note: The day’s fifth entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. **TWO CALENDARS, TWO DAYS, TEN DAYS APART.** This folder’s only other venerated row is the Greek one, on **19 July**, and this book keeps him on the **9th** — ten days apart, which is neither a thirteen-day conversion nor the same number. The `serbian` row was `undocumented`, so it is written plainly on this book’s day and **nothing of the Greek row is touched**. **THE FIRST DATE OF ANY KIND THIS FOLDER HAS HELD.** `dates` was **null**. This book says „Скончао 848. год.“ — he ended in the year 848. One book, one year, stated flat: `death` 848 to 848, display «848», basis traditional, and **nothing is widened** for want of a second year. **The two spans are refused**: „У 20 год. замонаши се и као монах провео 36 год.“ — tonsured in his twentieth year and thirty-six years a monk — is an age and a duration, and **nothing is subtracted from 848 to reach either a birth or a year of tonsure**, though the two numbers together would plainly offer one. A year derived by arithmetic is refused however well it would fit. WHAT IS NEW, WHICH IS THE WHOLE OF THE ENTRY. The tonsure at twenty and the thirty-six years as a monk; the election as bishop of Edessa „у време цара Михаила и Теодоре“, in the time of the emperor Michael and Theodora; and the year 848. `types` UNTOUCHED: `venerable`, `bishop` and `ascetic` are all three there; Свети is not a rank and „еп.“ is the `bishop`. `office` UNTOUCHED at «Bishop of Edessa», which is what the heading says. No `locations`: Edessa in a heading is not a coordinate. **NO NEW ROWS.** The folder already relates `michael-nephew-of-theodore-of-edessa`, whose display name carries this folder’s own name and whom this book does not mention. The emperor Michael and Theodora are an emperor and an empress in a life, which is not automatically a relation. **„и други с њим“ NAMES NOBODY, SO IT IS ONE ENTRY AND ONE ROW.** §4’s ruling on a synaxis heading decides it: one that enumerates its members is one folder per member, one that names nobody is one entry and the reader says so. Three men are named in the **body** and none of them takes a row: his teacher „св. Теодосије Столпник Сирски“ — `ls saints | grep -i theodosius-the-stylite` holds **nobody**, and an identification off a name in another man’s life is not an identification in any case; his brother „св. Јован“, a bare forename this corpus holds scores of times; and „св. Адер, племић и богаташ, који одбеже од жене и замонаши се“ — Ader, a nobleman and a rich man who fled from his wife and became a monk, for whom `ls saints | grep -i ader` returns three readers and no such man. A brother in a body is a kinship this reading cannot place on a folder it cannot find. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse.

death.note: The folder’s first date of any kind; `dates` was null before this reading. The Охридски пролог for 9. јул ст. ст.: „Скончао 848. год.“ — he ended in the year 848. One book, one year, stated flat, and nothing is widened for want of a second year to widen against. The same entry says he was tonsured in his twentieth year and spent thirty-six years as a monk: those are an age and a duration, not dates, and **nothing is subtracted from 848 to reach either a birth or a year of tonsure**, though the two numbers together would plainly offer one. The reign of the emperor Michael and Theodora, in which the entry puts his election, is no source for a year (6 October 2026).
